species.real: Derelict by the 1970s, the Albert Dock was restored in the 1980s and now holds Tate Liverpool, the Merseyside Maritime Museum and the International Slavery Museum.
species.name: Dockling

dex.text: A stocky little barnacled lump that hangs about the quays with its sleeves rolled up, waiting for a ship that needs unloading. Calls everyone 'la'.
dex.fact: Liverpool's Albert Dock opened in 1846. Its warehouses were built of cast iron, brick and stone with no wood in the structure, so they could not burn down.

species.real: Liverpool's waterfront, docks and all, was made a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004 and struck off in 2021 over new building, only the third site ever to lose the title.
species.name: Quayhulk

dex.text: Shoulders like a bollard and a back crusted with mussels. Can shift a crate the size of a terraced house, then sits down for a brew and does the crossword.
dex.fact: Monks from Birkenhead Priory rowed travellers across the Mersey in the Middle Ages, and King Edward III granted them the ferry rights in 1330.
